title: Obtaining purified human intestinal epithelia for single-cell analysis and organoid culture
protocol: Rinse human pediatric mucosal biopsies twice with PBS by removing the PBS and replacing it with fresh PBS.
Transfer sample to a pre-prepared six-well plate.
Place each sample in a separate well containing a total volume of 1.69 mL; HBSS (1.3 mL) with 1.07 Wünsch units/mL of Liberase DH (350 μL) and 600 IU of Hyaluronidase (40 μL).
Place the six-well plate on a shaker.
Incubate at 37°C for 15 min, rotating at 750 rpm.
Remove the six-well plate from the incubator after 15 min.
Mechanically disrupt the partially digested sample using a pre-coated p1000 pipette.
Pipette the entire mixture up and down several times to visibly reduce the structure of the biopsy without completely disappearing.
Place the six-well plate back into the incubator.
Rotate at 750 rpm in 37°C for an additional 15 min.
Remove the sample from the incubator.
Mechanically disrupt the sample by pipetting up and down approximately 10 times.
Transfer each disrupted sample to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the samples at 400 g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Dilute the pellet with 500 μL of DMEM/F-12.
Transfer the diluted sample to a 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge again at 400 g for 5 minutes.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Repeat the dilution and centrifugation steps once more.
Resuspend the sample in 1000 μL of DMEM/F-12.
Filter the resuspended sample through a 40 μm filter to remove debris or cell clumps.
Transfer the filtered sample to a 1.5 mL tube.
Store the tube on ice until required.
If utilizing the sample for single-cell RNA sequencing, filter the sample immediately before loading it into the machine utilized for single cell assessment.
Maintain the shortest time period possible between filtration and loading to prevent cell clumping.
Position the human fetal material supine in a cell culture hood.
Grip the abdominal wall near to the umbilicus with two forceps and gently pull the wall in opposite directions away from the midline.
Tear the abdominal wall until the abdominal contents are exposed.
Remove the liver by inserting forceps behind the superolateral aspect of the liver and everting it from the abdominal cavity.
Cut the biliary tree as close to the duodenum as possible to separate the liver and biliary system from the abdomen.
Identify the stomach and cut the stomach away from the esophagus carefully.
Remove the stomach from the abdominal cavity into a dish, ensuring that it remains connected to the duodenum.
Avoid gripping the intestine with forceps and use the stomach to mobilize the intestine.
Carefully pull the mesentery away from the intestine to dissect it from connective tissue/mesentery.
Cut the distal colon to separate entirely from the sample.
Remove remaining connective tissue/mesentery encasing the intestine by grasping two parts of the same section and pulling in opposite directions gently.
Repeat gentle separation until the intestine forms a single long tube.
Remove the stomach by cutting at the gastroduodenal junction.
Separate the colon by isolating the ileocecal junction and cutting at this site.
Further cut the small intestine to separate the duodenum/jejunum/ileum.
Transfer dissected pieces of gut to 0.5 mL of PBS and keep on ice until further processing.
Rinse twice with Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS) medium by replacing the PBS with 1 mL of HBSS, taking care not to remove any tissue and keeping sample on ice.
Place the tissue sample in HBSS medium containing Liberase DH and Hyaluronidase.
Incubate the plate on a shaking platform at 37°C for 15 min.
Pipette up and down using a P1000 pipette until the sample separates into a cellular solution.
Transfer each digested tissue sample to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the samples for 5 min at 400 g.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged samples.
Dilute the remaining pellet with 500 μL of DMEM and transfer to a 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge again for 5 min at 400 g.
Repeat the dilution step with an additional 500 μL of DMEM.
Resuspend the final pellet in 1000 μL of DMEM.
Filter through a 40 μm filter to remove debris or cell clusters.
Transfer the filtered sample to a 1.5 mL tube and store on ice until required.
Add 100 μl FcR Blocking Reagent to each tube.
Add 100 μl of CD326 (EpCAM) Microbeads per tube.
Mix well by pipetting.
Place the sample at 4°C for 30 min.
Add 5 ml running buffer to the sample.
Mix by pipetting and centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 600 μL of running buffer.
Load the sample onto an autoMACS machine and perform a “positive selection” automated cellular purification cycle.
Centrifuge the positively selected sample for 5 min at 400 g.
Resuspend the sample in 500 μL of DMEM/F-12.
Transfer the resuspended sample to a 1.5 mL tube.
Keep the sample on ice until further processing for single cell analysis or establishment of organoids.
Pass the suspension through a 40 μm filter immediately prior to use.
Remove the supernatant from cells.
Resuspend cell pellet in liquid Matrigel, using 20 μL per well plus 10% volume for each well.
Mix the Matrigel-cell solution thoroughly on ice.
Seed approximately 5,000 cells per well into the Matrigel mixture; aim to seed at least double this number with unsorted cells.
Maintain the gel and cells on ice during handling to prevent premature setting of Matrigel.
Transfer the mixed cell suspension in Matrigel onto a pre-warmed 48 well plate using 20 μL per well, ensuring the gel does not touch the sides of the wells.
Ensure the Matrigel/cell mix is kept on ice as much as possible.
Pipette the Matrigel/cell mix into a 48-well plate while keeping it cold.
Invert the plate and place it in the incubator for five minutes.
Once the Matrigel has set, pipette 200-250 μL of intestinal organoid medium onto each well.
Change the medium 24 hours later and every 48 hours thereafter.
Tilt the plate to 45° when changing the medium.
Use a pipette to remove the medium from the bottom edge of the well carefully.
Avoid disturbing or disrupting the Matrigel dome during medium changes.
Pre-warm medium to 37°C before use.
Apply pre-warmed medium slowly to the bottom of the well without disturbing the Matrigel dome.
Passage organoids every 5–10 days either mechanically or via enzymatic digestion as needed.
Scrape the Matrigel dome off the surface of the plate using a p1000 pipette for mechanical passage.
Pipette up the gel together with the medium into a 1.5 mL tube.
Press the tip of the pipette into the bottom of the tube to flatten it.
Pipette the gel/media mix several times to break up organoids.
Centrifuge the mixture at 400 g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant from the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in the desired volume of gel at a ratio of 1:6 wells, with a total gel volume of 20 μL per well plus 10%.
Pipette 20 μL of gel to each well of a pre-warmed 48 well plate.
Invert the plate quickly and place it in the incubator for five minutes.
Once the Matrigel has set (approximately five minutes at 37°C), pipette 200–250 μL of pre-warmed intestinal organoid medium onto each well.
Change the medium 24 hours later, and subsequently every 48 hours.
Maintain the organoids in this manner for over one year if required.
To cryopreserve organoids, remove the media from four wells.
Replace with 1 mL of cell recovery solution (250 μL per well).
Transfer the gel and cell recovery solution to a 1.5 mL tube and keep on ice for 20 minutes.
Centrifuge at 400 g for five minutes.
Remove the supernatant and wash in basal medium twice.
Re-suspend the pellet in 500 μL of freeing medium.
Place the sample in a freezing container.
Transfer the container to a −80°C freezer.
After 48–72 hours, transfer the sample to liquid nitrogen for storage.
To thaw the organoids, place the vial into a water bath at 37°C.
Once thawed, wash the organoids three times in basal medium.
Resuspend the organoids in Matrigel and re-plate with an appropriate volume of medium.
Remove the organoid medium and replace with 200 μL of Cell Recovery Solution.
Using a p1000 pipette, scrape the gel off the bottom of the plate.
Pipette up with the cell recovery solution and transfer to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Incubate on ice for 20 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample at 400 g for five minutes.
If Matrigel has not fully dissolved, maintain on ice for further five minutes and repeat.
Remove the supernatant after centrifugation.
Re-suspend in 500 μL of pre-warmed TrypLE.
Incubate for 10 minutes in a water bath at 37°C.
Assess the sample under a microscope to determine if further incubation is required.
Add 500 μL of refrigerated DMEM.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend in 500 μL of DMEM (4°C).
Repeat the previous three steps for a total of three times.
Filter the cells through a 40 μm filter.
